extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors submitting manuscripts to Pan Macmillan India (agented or unsolicited)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and sending a manuscript submission to Pan Macmillan India, including what genres are considered, required documents and formats, evaluation criteria, timelines, and post-submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/subject connection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At Pan Macmillan India we accept manuscripts that have a strong connection to India or the Indian subcontinent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We look at publishing stories that have a strong connection to India and the Indian subcontinent, irrespective of the nationality of the author. If your submission is set outside the Indian context, consider sending it to one of our international trade publishing arms (Pan Macmillan USA, Africa, Australia, Picador UK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted fiction categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction accepted: modern contemporary fiction, horror, historical fiction, thriller and suspense, historical thrillers, fantasy, literary fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We do not focus on campus-oriented, college romance. The listed categories are examples we accept but submissions are not limited to these.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted general and narrative non-fiction categories
rubrics_metrics.description: General and narrative non-fiction accepted: self-help; current affairs; sports; fitness and diet; business and management; family and health; popular philosophy; anthologies; travel writing; cultural studies; literary essays; social sciences; politics and government; history; memoirs; epidemiology; biographies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the non-fiction areas we commonly publish, but submissions are not strictly limited to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded genres and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Pan Macmillan India does not publish school and college textbooks. Poetry submissions are not accepted at present. Short stories, illustrated books, graphic novels and textbooks are not published. We do not look at children's books or illustrated stories for young readers and graphic novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry may be considered in future—check for updates. If in doubt about format, see Macmillan Education for educational/reference queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent vs unsolicited submission priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts sent through a literary agent will receive a higher priority. However, we also accept unsolicited submissions which may be sent by email to paneditorial@macmillan.co.in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an agent increases priority but is not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission contents
rubrics_metrics.description: For our evaluation process please send us the following: a short synopsis of your work (500 words); a brief outline of the chapters; only the first three sample chapters (please do not send chapters of a random number sequence); a short note about yourself with relevant details (employment status, any other published work); a short note on ideas about target audience, age group, why the book will work and what will make it stand out; mention comparable titles in the market if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not send the complete copy of your manuscript at this stage. Ideas for book covers are also not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send the documents as separate, attached MS Word files that are not password protected. Manuscripts should be typed in Times New Roman, in black font on white page (font size 12 and double-spaced). Do not send PDF documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the specified format and do not use unreadable fonts, colour, highlights etc. Ensure legibility of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to send (submission channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only through email. Please send your submissions only by email to paneditorial@macmillan.co.in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send hard copies of manuscripts. We do not return manuscripts sent through mail, irrespective of the final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: You can expect to hear from us within three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We receive many submissions and the process takes a while. During this period we would appreciate if you do not call or send reminder mails; it becomes difficult to respond to individual mails while handling a large number of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria used by editors
rubrics_metrics.description: We evaluate a manuscript on several parameters like style, content, readability, market trends and sales potential. Whether the manuscript fits our publishing programme is also a crucial factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors assess manuscripts in the context of other manuscripts and previously published books—consider competition in the market and whether other books execute a similar idea more adeptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to do if no response in three months
rubrics_metrics.description: In the rare event that you do not receive a response from us within three months, please send us a reminder which includes the initial date of your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will then respond to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: If editorial interest is generated
rubrics_metrics.description: If your submission generates interest then our editorial team will ask for the full manuscript. This does not imply that your manuscript has been accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will be a detailed evaluation of the entire manuscript; it may be returned with feedback and editorial inputs and suggestions. You may work on suggestions and resend; upon a second evaluation, if it meets standards we will send an offer for publishing the work. Inform us if you have submitted your work elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: No in-person submissions or meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Please refrain from sending a hard copy of your manuscript or delivering it in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doing so does not increase chances of acceptance of the submission. Send a soft copy according to guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfinished work / proposals not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept proposals; please write in to us only when you have a finished manuscript with you, though you do not need to send it right away but we may ask for it if your submission generates interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send outlines in lieu of finished work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You can send your manuscript for evaluation to other publishers as well. However, please mention clearly in the email if you’ve sent your work for evaluation elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, if your manuscript is accepted by another publishing house while we are evaluating it, let us know immediately so that we can discontinue the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts once rejected will not be looked at again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not resend the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback availability
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive an email when the editors complete evaluating your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, with the large number of submissions we receive, it is not possible to give an individual feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance about idea theft
rubrics_metrics.description: We value the immense faith that we have received from authors and readers alike. It is strictly against our value system as a leading publishing house to indulge in idea theft or any form of unethical/unprofessional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an assurance rather than an evaluative criterion; it explains the publisher's stance on author intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your manuscript has been accepted, the publishing process takes up to 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on length of the manuscript and the editorial changes required, the time period may be shorter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author role in marketing and promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: On acceptance of submission, the author will be guided through a detailed procedure outlining the marketing and promotional program of Pan Macmillan India by our marketing team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best results are achieved when the author and the publisher work in tandem to market the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial/royalty queries handled after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Queries related to marketing, royalties, distribution etc. are discussed in depth once the manuscript has been accepted to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is too early to consider these at the initial stage of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript originality and plagiarism policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure that the submission sent to us is your original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have quoted material from another text or author, please mention the sources in footnotes or in a separate Word Document. A failure to do so will automatically amount to plagiarism and subsequent rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation, proofreading, and cover letter importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof-read your manuscript for errors of spelling, punctuation, paragraphs, page numbering, indent, grammar, spacing, typography etc. Attach all documents as separate MS Word files and give necessary details including your name and contact. The cover letter is a crucial document and the editors examine it closely before looking at your manuscript. Address the cover letter to the Evaluations Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure synopsis is concise and avoids unnecessary details; adhere to word limits for synopsis/author profile; check font style, spacing and colouring; once complete, ask yourself ‘Did I enjoy my work as a reader?’ or ‘Would I recommend my work to others to read?’

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript retention and liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Please retain a copy of your work. Pan Macmillan India will not be liable for any loss or damage to the submitted work nor will the company return manuscripts to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send original copies you cannot replace.
